title: P25 wider residual stream, narrower MLP at the 10M cap: d_model 384 -> 448 (8 heads of 56) with d_ff 1280 -> 896 (2x) in all six Peri-LN blocks on the 153-claude incumbent (9,770,880 params)
description: P25 (wider residual stream, narrower MLP): widen the 153-claude incumbent's residual stream and attention from 384 to 448 (8 heads of 56: 4 ALiBi slopes 1/4..1/256 + 4 NoPE) and pay for it at the 10M cap by cutting the MLP from 1280 (3.33x) to 896 (2x), giving 9,770,880 params (+2.2%); depth, heads, slopes, MTP module, optimizers, schedule and token-budget batches are unchanged. Residual width was the lever in 151 (+13.7) and 153 (+14.7, MLP held), while 154-fable3's wider q/k/v alone did nothing and 124's 3x-vs-4x MLP was neutral, so moving parameters from MLP to residual width should give expert iteration a better sampler at the same parameter count.
hypothesis: At the 10M cap the recipe is still capacity-shaped rather than step-limited (val loss bottoms mid-run and rises over ~4 epochs; 153's +28% params cost -5.4% steps and gained +14.7 with round-1 targets solved +70%). The gains of 151/153 came from the residual stream (and the proj/fc1 inputs that read it), not from q/k/v width alone (154-fable3: 1.4x attention width at residual 320 changed nothing), while MLP expansion has looked neutral (124: 3x vs 4x at 256 tied with 16% fewer params). A 448-wide residual stream carries more proof-state features per token (names, premises, goal shape) and 56-dim NoPE heads carry more identity per key for citation lookup; the 2x MLP gives back parameters the overfit, memorization-heavy regime has in excess. Expert iteration then starts from a better sampler and transfers better to length >= 7. Risks: 2x MLP is below any ratio tested under Lean; bench shows ~10% fewer steps (10.35 vs 11.53 steps/s over the first 60 s); one-seed sd ~44 swamps a small gain; diminishing returns past 384.
expected_delta: -45 to +40 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean), central +3; keep needs > 687.00 (153-claude: 676/700/685). Mechanism predictions: pretraining steps 3,700-4,400 per seed (central ~4,050 = 153's 4,503 x the bench ratio 0.90), falsified if the mean is < 3,400; epochs 3.2-3.9; final main val loss 0.078-0.094 (153: 0.087-0.089); round-1 targets solved mean >= 550 (153: 766/747/694), a falsifier of 'better sampler' if below 450; round-4 RL-solved 1,120-1,210 (153: 1,157-1,191); totals 1,600-2,100 s (153: 1,741); RL sampling >= 200 samples/s (153: 225-256).

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 153-claude except width; PeriLNBlock replaces the fork Block's 4*D fc1/fc2 with Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 896 (2 x 448)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 153-claude: knob line N_LAYER, D, N_HEAD = 6, 384, 8 -> 6, 448, 8 and D_FF 1280 -> 896 (comment updated); no other line changed. Derived from D: head dim 48 -> 56 (8 heads: 4 ALiBi slopes 1/4..1/256 + 4 NoPE, unchanged table), embedding/readout width 448, MTP module width 448 (proj (448, 896), its block also d_ff 896), Muon shape scale sqrt(max(rows, cols) / 448): Q/K/V/proj/head 1, fc1/fc2 sqrt(896/448) = 1.41 (153: 1.83), MTP proj sqrt(2). 896 != 3*448 = 1344, so muon_step's QKV-by-shape test still splits only qkv. Loss, optimizers, schedule, init rule, token batches (TOK_BUDGET 18,432) and handoff unchanged.
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,770,880 (hand count, and bench_pretrain on an A40 reported the same; per Peri-LN block 1,612,352 = qkv 603,456 + proj 201,152 + fc1 402,304 + fc2 401,856 + 4 LayerNorms 3,584; emb + head 95,872; ln_f 896). MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff as since 136-fable): 2,015,552 (2 input LayerNorms 1,792 + proj 401,408 + one Peri-LN block 1,612,352); pretraining trains 11,786,432 in total; the harness caps the handed-off model's parameters (9.77M), which is what RL and eval use
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 448, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 896), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged code path from 153 (caches[0] holds key positions); only widths differ

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (448,896) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 153)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 448 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (896,448) and fc2 (448,896) sqrt(896/448) = 1.41, head (107,448) 1, MTP proj (448,896) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1344,448) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151/153 (same 30 as 153; bench_pretrain ran muon_step at this shape)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,448,448), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (896,448) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (448,896): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,770,880

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151/153: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 448; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: unchanged code from 136/153; their CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence): 624 steps in 60.3 s = 10.35 steps/s (153-claude's shape: 11.53), peak 8.47 GB (153: 7.42), n_params 9,770,880, sampling 214 samples/s (153's bench: 179), sample_acc 0.080
